area: Task 28 Phase 2 — authoring preview refresh architecture (prototyped and measured, nothing shipped)
findings: PROBLEM CONFIRMED on the real artifact. data/linear.app/recon-templates/2026-08-25T21-53-26-980Z/app/src/runtime/slot-content.ts:92 `let contractPromise: Promise<Map<string, ResolvedOp[]>> | null = null;` plus :138-141 `getContract() { if (!contractPromise) contractPromise = buildContract(); ... }` memoizes the whole content contract for the process lifetime, and load-page.ts:18 `const cache = new Map<string, Promise<RuntimePage>>();` caches each page tree AFTER applySlotContent() has already mutated it. The generated header comment at slot-content.ts:17-20 says it outright: 'change a value, restart the server'. Writing a new WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE has zero effect on a running `next start`.

BONUS, load-bearing for any patch strategy: src/runtime/slot-content.ts and src/runtime/load-page.ts are BYTE-IDENTICAL between the linear.app 2026-08-25T21-53-26-980Z template run and the stripe.com 2026-08-18T10-45-40-007Z run (verified by string compare). One guarded patch with the same anchor discipline as src/production/patch.ts generalizes across template generations.

CANDIDATE C's flight-payload question is ANSWERED EMPIRICALLY AND NEGATIVELY FOR HTML-ONLY. Rewriting only outside <script> elements produced React error #418 (hydration text mismatch) in headless Chromium AND the value REVERTED: 0 new occurrences / 4 old occurrences in the live DOM after hydration, htmlHits=2. Rewriting HTML + the inline self.__next_f.push flight chunks gave 4/4 new occurrences, 0 old, 0 hydration errors, 0 js errors. So src/seo/serve.ts's dual (head + flight) rewrite is load-bearing, not belt-and-braces.

CANDIDATE C DOES NOT GENERALISE TO ARBITRARY SLOT TEXT — measured on the linear template (2441 text slots, 1790 distinct default values, 9929 bindings): 828 text slots (34%) share their default value with at least one other slot, so a needle cannot address one of them; 292 distinct default values are a SUBSTRING of another default value (live example: slot `teams and agents` is a substring of the hero headline `The product development system for teams and agents`); and occurrence over-reach on the served homepage is severe — `Performance` has 6 bindings but 16 raw occurrences, `In Progress` 6 vs 12, `Purpose-built` 4 vs 16, `teams and agents` 1 binding vs 20 raw occurrences. Substitution also discards the Slot V2 expectedValue guard entirely, and 2432 static/attribute + 64 dynamic-template/attribute bindings would be rewritten wherever the string appears (CSS, JS, URLs included).

CANDIDATE B IS CORRECT, NOT JUST FAST. With WR_AUTHORING_HOT unset, the patched app's HTML across all 8 linear routes differs from the unpatched app by exactly 150 characters on every route — all of them Next's own build identity (chunk filenames `chunks/<hash>.js`, module ids `I[<n>,`, and the buildId `b:"<id>"`). After normalizing only those three, all 8 routes are byte-identical. Under WR_AUTHORING_HOT=1: 4/4 bound occurrences updated, no stale default left, 0 `[wr-slot]` guard warnings across every run, and a revert to the default value restored 4/4 occurrences exactly (50 ms).

THEME NEEDS NO NEXT RESTART, BUT THE EXISTING PROXY IS COLD. src/theme/serve.ts:62 `const overlayBytes = Buffer.from("\n" + overlayCss)` captures the CSS at startOverlayProxy() time — measured: after editing the overlay file the proxy still served the old epoch (stillServesOldEpoch=true, fileEditVisibleWithoutProxyRestart=false). Restarting only the proxy costs 23 ms median / 25 ms max (n=5). An mtime-gated per-request re-read makes it fully hot at 19 ms median / 20 ms max (n=5) with no restart at all, and theme edit -> browser-visible via a <link> swap with no navigation is 126 ms median / 239 ms max (n=5), 0 js errors, 0 hydration errors.

THE IMAGE HOT SEAM IS REAL ON THE SERVER AND DEAD IN THE BROWSER. src/assets/serve.ts:85 does read each media file from disk per request — confirmed, 5/5 fetches saw the new bytes at 0 ms median / 1 ms max, no next restart and no proxy restart. But the same handler sends `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`: across 5 file replacements followed by 5 full page reloads, the proxy received ZERO media requests and the rendered pixel stayed at the stale value (10,20,30) every single time. With a cache-bust query token and an img.src swap (no navigation), 5/5 reps showed the correct new pixel at 2 ms median / 2 ms max with exactly 1 proxy hit each.

THE BASELINE BEING AVOIDED, measured not assumed: a static-export `next build` of the production-patched app (src/production/patch.ts applied verbatim) took 3277 ms, and the last real recorded bake at data/linear.app/production-builds/2026-08-26T19-26-48-957Z/report/bake-report.json reports nextBuildMs 2734, routeHtmlFiles 10, siteFileCount 215, siteBytes 258657907 in a 348 MB run directory. That is the per-keystroke cost Phase 3 is eliminating.

SCALE HOLDS. Repeating the winner on the stripe.com template (20 routes, 9529 slots, 24518 bindings, largest page JSON 1.9 MB): clean `next build` 2886 ms, edit->visible 101 ms median / 109 ms max (n=6), 0 `[wr-slot]` warnings. Candidate A on the same site: 444 ms median / 458 ms max (n=5). The ~4x gap is stable across site sizes.

options.name: A — worker restart (kill and re-spawn `next start` on the prebuilt .next)
options.howItWorks: Write the new WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE, SIGTERM the running `next start`, spawn a new one on a fresh ephemeral port, poll until the new text appears. This is exactly what src/recon-template/parity-qa.ts:130 already does, so it needs no source change at all. Because the port changes on every restart I had to put a stable-URL front proxy with connect-retry in front of it before a browser could be pointed at a fixed preview URL — that proxy is mandatory work, not optional polish.
options.measured: linear.app (8 routes, prebuilt .next, appA): cold start ready 316 ms, cold first page 385 ms. Server-side edit->visible n=5, median 393 ms, max 398 ms, min 392 ms (all: 394/393/393/392/398). stripe.com (20 routes, appSA): cold ready 330 ms, cold first page 452 ms, edit->visible n=5, median 444 ms, max 458 ms. Browser-measured edit->visible (stable front proxy, page.reload, waitForFunction on the new text) n=5: median 578 ms, max 608 ms, min 569 ms. Playwright: 0 console/pageerror js errors, 0 hydration errors. Server RSS after warming all 8 routes: 192 MB.
options.cost: Zero source changes and zero build. Requires a stable-URL front proxy (~80 lines) because the port moves. Every restart drops in-flight requests and throws away the warm page cache, so the first render after each edit re-reads and re-parses every page again.
options.risk: LOW correctness risk, HIGH interaction-latency risk. It is 7.4x slower than B server-side (393 vs 53 ms) and 2.9x slower browser-side (578 vs 199 ms), and the gap is a hard floor: ~320 ms of it is Node/Next process boot, which no amount of tuning removes. It cannot ever feel like a keystroke.

options.name: B — overlay indirection / env-gated cache bypass (RECOMMENDED for text)
options.howItWorks: Two guarded patches on the generated runtime, both dead unless WR_AUTHORING_HOT=1. In slot-content.ts: an authoring EPOCH = `${mtimeMs}:${size}` of the WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE, exposed as `slotContentEpoch()`; a changed epoch sets `contractPromise = null`. In load-page.ts: cache the raw page JSON TEXT once per process, and key the applied trees on `pageFile|epoch`, evicting the page's other epochs. A fresh JSON.parse per epoch is REQUIRED, not an optimisation — applySlotContent mutates the tree in place and its own expectedValue guard would refuse a second application to an already-written tree. Nothing is patched on the client; the server simply renders the new tree. Prototype at tmp/wr28/proto-preview/patch-b.mjs, applied to appB/appBcold/appS.
options.measured: One-time `next build`: 1886 ms with the .next carried over from the copy, 3180 ms from a clean .next (linear), 2886 ms clean (stripe). Startup: cold ready 324 ms, cold first page 395 ms. linear.app server-side edit->visible n=8: median 53 ms, max 59 ms, min 49 ms (59/52/50/50/53/53/53/49) — served correctly on the FIRST request every time (attempts=1, never a retry). With a 500-key overlay n=6: median 55 ms, max 64 ms. First render after an edit, per route, all 8 routes: 29-55 ms. Revert-to-default: 50 ms, 4/4 occurrences restored, no stale value. stripe.com n=6: median 101 ms, max 109 ms. Browser-measured edit->visible n=5: median 199 ms, max 269 ms, min 184 ms. Playwright: 0 js errors, 0 hydration errors, 4/4 occurrences, staleDefaultLeft=false, 0 [wr-slot] server warnings. Non-hot parity: all 8 routes differ by exactly 150 chars, 100% Next build identity, byte-identical after normalizing chunk hashes + module ids + buildId. Server RSS after warming 8 routes: 230 MB (+38 MB vs unpatched).
options.cost: One `next build` per template before authoring can start (2.9-3.2 s clean) — real, but paid once, not per keystroke. +38 MB RSS per live preview from the raw-page-text cache. Two new guarded patches to maintain alongside the four already in src/production/patch.ts.
options.risk: MEDIUM-LOW, with one named defect in the prototype that MUST be fixed before shipping. src/production/patch.ts `patchSlotContent` still applies cleanly to the patched file (verified by actually calling it: anchors intact, baked marker written), BUT my `readEpoch()` reuses the literal `process.env.WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE`, so that string survives into the baked artifact and textually contradicts the bake's own doctrine comment ('No environment variable is consulted — the runtime has no external run-directory dependency'). At runtime the baked export is unaffected (WR_AUTHORING_HOT is unset, readEpoch is never called), but Phase 3 must either use a distinct env var for the epoch source or add a fifth guarded patch that strips the authoring block. Second, smaller risk: the epoch is (mtimeMs,size), so two writes in the same millisecond with the same byte length would not invalidate — a monotonic counter or content hash inside the overlay file removes that hole.

options.name: C — proxy substitution (reverse proxy rewriting values in the response)
options.howItWorks: A reverse proxy in front of an unmodified `next start`, following src/theme/serve.ts / src/seo/serve.ts / src/assets/serve.ts. It buffers each text/html and text/x-component response and runs the repo's own applySubstitutionVariants (src/seo/escape-variants.ts) for every from->to pair, replacing each encoding of the needle with the same encoding of the replacement. An edit is an in-memory Map write — no file, no restart, no build.
options.measured: Fastest of the three. Cold ready 323 ms, cold first page 401 ms. Server-side edit->visible n=8: median 33 ms, max 42 ms, min 31 ms (42/34/37/33/31/33/33/31), 4/4 occurrences rewritten and 4 substitution hits per response. Browser-measured n=5: median 173 ms, max 233 ms, 0 js errors, 0 hydration errors. Flight experiment (the decisive one): HTML-only rewriting -> 1 hydration error (React #418, args[]=text), 0 new occurrences and 4 old occurrences surviving in the live DOM, i.e. the value visibly REVERTED; HTML+flight -> 4 new / 0 old, 0 hydration errors. Generalisation measured against the real slot table: 828/2441 text slots (34%) share a default value with another slot; 292 default values are a substring of another; on the served homepage `Performance` = 6 bindings vs 16 raw occurrences, `In Progress` 6 vs 12, `Purpose-built` 4 vs 16, `teams and agents` 1 binding vs 20 occurrences.
options.cost: No source change to the template app, no build, no restart. But it needs a full-body buffer of every HTML response (2.4-2.7 MB per linear page) and an N-needle pass over it for every request, and every additional edited slot adds another full-document pass.
options.risk: HIGH and disqualifying for slot content. It has no addressing: it substitutes a STRING, while Slot V2 addresses an OCCURRENCE (pageId/viewport/surface/nodeId/childIndex) and verifies expectedValue before writing. The 34% duplicate-value rate and 292 substring containments are not edge cases — editing `teams and agents` would silently corrupt the hero headline that contains it, and editing `Performance` would rewrite 16 places instead of the 6 that are bound. It throws away exactly the invariant slot-content.ts:20-24 exists to protect. It remains correct and should be kept for its current job: strings that are unique per document, which is why src/seo/serve.ts uses it for <title>.

recommendation: SHIP A HYBRID, and the split is not a compromise — each layer already has a different natural seam. (1) TEXT / SLOT CONTENT -> Candidate B. It is the only candidate that preserves Slot V2 addressing and the expectedValue guard while getting under the interaction threshold: 53 ms median server-side and 199 ms median in a real browser on linear, 101 ms server-side on stripe, versus 393/578 ms for A and versus a 2734-3277 ms production bake. Its one-time price is a single `next build` (2886-3180 ms clean) and +38 MB RSS, and it is provably inert when off — all 8 routes byte-identical to the unpatched app after normalizing Next's own build identity, with the production bake patch still applying. Before shipping, fix the one named defect: give the epoch its own env var (or add a fifth guarded patch stripping the authoring block) so `process.env.WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE` does not survive into the baked artifact, and consider a monotonic counter instead of (mtimeMs,size). (2) THEME -> keep the existing overlay proxy (src/theme/serve.ts), change only the one line that freezes the CSS at startup into an mtime-gated per-request re-read. No Next restart is ever needed for a theme edit because the HTML is byte-identical by construction: 19 ms to serve, 126 ms to browser-visible via a <link> swap with no navigation. (3) IMAGES -> the existing per-request disk read at src/assets/serve.ts:85 really is the hot seam and needs no architectural change, but it is currently unusable from a browser because its own `cache-control: immutable` gave 0 refetches across 5 reloads and a permanently stale pixel. The whole fix is authoring-mode cache headers plus a cache-bust token on img.src: 2 ms, 5/5 correct. (4) Keep Candidate A as the correctness reference and the fallback when WR_AUTHORING_HOT is unavailable — it is already what parity-qa does and it is hydration-clean, just too slow to type against. (5) REJECT Candidate C for slot content on measured evidence, and keep it exactly where it already lives: document-unique strings such as <title>. The Phase-3 preview server is therefore: `next start` with WR_AUTHORING_HOT=1 behind one stable-URL proxy that (a) forwards, (b) appends theme CSS re-read on mtime, (c) serves /media per-request with no-store in authoring mode — and a stable preview URL the editor iframe never has to change.
risks: PROTOTYPE DEFECT, must be fixed before Phase 3 ships B: readEpoch() in my patch reuses the literal `process.env.WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE`, so that string survives src/production/patch.ts's patchSlotContent into the baked artifact and textually breaks the bake's 'no environment variable is consulted' doctrine. Runtime behaviour of the export is unaffected (WR_AUTHORING_HOT is unset so readEpoch never runs) but the doctrine claim would become false. Verified by calling patchSlotContent on both the pristine and the patched file: both apply, but 'env seam removed' is true for pristine and FALSE for the patched one.

The B epoch is (mtimeMs, size). Two overlay writes in the same millisecond producing the same byte length would not invalidate the contract. It never fired in 8+6+5+6 measured reps, but it is a real hole; a monotonic counter or content hash written into the overlay file closes it.

ALL B numbers are FULL-PAGE-RELOAD numbers. I prototyped no partial, streaming, or diff-based DOM update. Each invalidation re-parses the entire page JSON (1.4 MB linear home, 1.9 MB stripe), so an un-debounced keystroke-rate editor would re-parse per keystroke. Debouncing is Phase 3's problem and I did not measure it.

The hot path was exercised end-to-end only on STATIC TEXT bindings. dynamic-template (data-wr-obs) bindings — 198 text + 64 attribute in the linear template — and paint-twin and svg-text bindings were not driven through B's re-parse cycle. The parity-qa mutation canary covers those for the restart path, not for the epoch-keyed path. Phase 3 must add that coverage before trusting B for the portal/menu surfaces.

Concurrency was not measured at all: one preview server, one browser, one editor. Multi-tenant capacity (192 MB unpatched / 230 MB patched RSS per live server) and simultaneous editors are unmeasured.

Every number is single-machine: darwin 25.2.0, APFS, Node 22, next 16.3.0, headless chromium, 127.0.0.1 loopback, no network latency, no CPU contention beyond whatever other Task-28 phases were doing concurrently. Absolute milliseconds will differ elsewhere; the ratios between candidates are the durable result.

The A-vs-B comparison used the SAME prebuilt .next for A (appA, copied from the frozen template run) but a REBUILT .next for B. B's rebuild is genuinely required by its patch, and the 150-character diff proves the rebuild changed nothing but Next's build identity — but it does mean A and B were not served from bit-identical bundles.

I made no source changes, ran no smoke suite and no typecheck, so I hold no evidence about regression counts and I took the suite mutex zero times. Nothing was appended to docs/result/handoffs/28-intel/pending-package-scripts.tsv: this is a prototype, there is nothing to register. All work is confined to /Users/woops/projects/web-recon/tmp/wr28/proto-preview/ (507 MB of scratch app copies); a `find -newermt` check confirms zero files were modified in any historical data/ run directory.
